target.title: Guard AWS raw instance release by ownership tags
target.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/703.

## Summary

- reject direct AWS raw `i-*` resolution unless the instance carries the canonical `crabbox=true`, `created_by=crabbox`, `provider=aws`, canonical lease ID, and non-empty slug ownership tags
- validate the resolved lease ID against the ownership tag before release and recheck canonical ownership at the provider delete boundary
- skip and report noncanonical inventory entries during cleanup so one unowned instance cannot block cleanup of later valid leases
- deliberately fail closed for unmanaged raw EC2 IDs in every resolution mode because ordinary connect/status flows can mutate lifecycle tags
- add regression coverage and an Unreleased changelog entry thanking @TurboTheTurtle

## Verification

Current exact head: `06fc951175cd9248552214ea3fa397939427bb3f`.

- `go test -race ./internal/providers/aws`
- `go test -race ./internal/providers/aws ./internal/cli`
- `go vet ./...`
- `git diff --check`
- autoreview accepted two findings, fixed both, then completed clean with no actionable findings; patch correct at 0.82 confidence

## Remaining live gate

Use a newly created disposable Crabbox-owned instance only:

1. create it from this exact head
2. remove one canonical ownership tag
3. prove raw-ID stop is rejected and the instance remains running
4. restore the tag
5. stop it normally and verify instance/key cleanup and zero residue

Do not use an existing external instance. The configured AWS profiles currently fail `sts:GetCallerIdentity` with `InvalidClientTokenId`; live proof is waiting only on an unlocked valid credential from 1Password.
